text:
Happy Thursday! It's another mild, muggy morning, and a round of showers is moving in from the west. Expect on and off rain from about 7 this morning into the early afternoon, heaviest between 8 and 10. It's not a soaker, though. Most of us will see only around a tenth of an inch, with a brief downpour possible near midday. A south wind will be gusty too, with gusts near 30 mph. Highs land near 68, a little cooler than Wednesday.

Showers turn more scattered this evening and wrap up around 11, and a rumble of thunder isn't out of the question. The Euro and one other model are wetter than the official forecast today, so keep the umbrella handy until bedtime. Tonight stays mild, with a low around 51.

Friday looks mostly dry and partly sunny, with a high near 64 and a light northeast breeze. One model hints at a spot shower, but I'd bet on dry. Enjoy it, because the weekend turns showery and much cooler, with highs back near 50 on Saturday.

AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: Anomalous moisture, with PWAT more than 200% of normal, and likely near record for the date per Albany, NY sounding climatology, will be present today as a slug of showers slides northeastward across the region this morning. Despite this impressive moisture and very warm air in place, rainfall looks meager as forcing for ascent is weak given a lagging shortwave trough and lack of frontogenesis. That said, low to mid-level lapse rates look to be sufficient for some instability and brief downpours in some of the showers, especially towards midday which helps southern and eastern portions of Vermont have better odds of these heavier showers. Think these will be brief such that total rainfall amounts in a given hour will at most be about 0.25" and mainly up to 0.1". After this swath of showers and deep moisture exits to our east, partial clearing will support some warm season type of heating and skinny CAPE profiles that bring us a non-zero chance of thunderstorms towards evening. HRRR/RRFS guidance has been consistent in showing a broken line of showers forming in northern New York and gradually translating eastward with increasing MUCAPE, progged to reach about 200-300 J/kg. Chances of thunder in the calibrated REFS data is surprisingly high in far northern Vermont (around 30-40%) based on this CAPE. Greatest chances of a rumble of thunder appears to be during the mid- afternoon near Route 11 in northern New York and then during the evening in eastern Franklin County in Vermont. Most of the remainder of the night, aside from this possible cluster of showers exiting to the east, will be dry and mild. Much of Friday continues to look dry and unseasonably warm despite being a bit cooler than today. KEY MESSAGE 2: We continue to expect an unsettled weather pattern for the weekend, as a closed upper level low ambles eastward from the eastern Great Lakes Friday night into the Gulf of Maine by Sunday afternoon. Its slow movement will provide a prolonged period of shower chances across the region, but it remains hard to pinpoint where/when rain showers will pivot across a particular location. Generally Saturday afternoon through Saturday night looks like the timeframe where showers should be most abundant over northern New York and Vermont given the proximity of this system, and the track will favor southern portions of our region with regards to rainfall amounts. While a big soaking rain is not expected, a wetting rainfall of 0.25" through the weekend has increased a bit to a 50-65% chance, while rainfall in excess of 1" is now about 10-15%, except 20-25% in portions of western Vermont in the Winooski and Mad River Valleys and the western Adirondack region. With the expected low pressure track, we also should see some increasing northerly flow towards late Saturday but there isn't much cold air to advect in. WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) -Happy Thursday! A round of rain showers looks to roll through from west to east this morning into the early afternoon. Another round of showers may pop up here and there through this evening and into the first part of tonight. Right now, it looks like we all see rain, but it’s not a ton with most only getting a couple tenths of an inch of new rain. Temperatures are a tad cooler with most in the low to mid 60s. Friday looks drier, but there could still be a spotty shower here and there. We continue to lose a little ground temperature-wise, as most areas talk high temperatures in the upper 50s and lower 60s. The weekend could again feature a few showers for Saturday. Temperatures turn noticeably cooler with most only in the 40s to about 50 for Saturday afternoon. Sunday looks drier, but could feature a spotty morning shower or two. Temperatures are generally stuck in the 40s for most. We’ll keep the clouds and a few spotty showers going into next week. There could even be a few mountain snowflakes from time to time Monday and Tuesday. While clouds and a few passing showers are present through the end of this week and into the upcoming weekend and to start next week, no one day looks to be a washout, and rain amounts top out at about 0.75″.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-04T21:02:00Z — same caveat): Rain arrives Thursday, remaining mild and muggy — Several towns broke record highs on Wednesday as temperatures soared into the 70s. Tonight will feel very spring-like, as we hang out close to 60 degrees. Thursday stays mild, with highs in the mid-upper 60s. An approaching cold front brings a mostly cloudy sky and scattered showers. A late evening or overnight thunderstorm cannot be ruled out in southern Vermont. The south breeze becomes a bit stronger, with gusts near 30. Friday turns drier, with only a spot shower leftover. A few hours of sunshine are likely, but New York will remain cloudier overall. Highs again reach the 60s. This weekend turns much cooler, an an upper-level low sends highs back closer to 50. Expect lots of clouds with a few additional showers, especially on Saturday.
